title: tcpdump BPF basics and text output
shortTitle: 11 — tcpdump BPF basics and text output
intro: Work from the module directory. Parse **`tcpdump_nn_sample.txt`** only.

questions.prompt: How many lines contain **`443`** anywhere? Print **only** the integer.
How many lines contain **`UDP`**? Print **only** the integer.
How many TCP **connection-initiation** packets (SYN, not SYN-ACK) appear in the capture? Print **only** the integer.
How many packets carry a **data-push** (PSH flag set with ACK) in the capture? Print **only** the integer.
How many **connection-reset** packets appear in the capture? Print **only** the integer.
How many lines contain **`127.0.0.1`**? Print **only** the integer.
Count lines containing **`> 198.51.100.22.`** (destination begins with that prefix). Print **only** the integer.
Consider only lines containing **`UDP`**. For each, print the **destination IPv4** (dotted quad after **`>`** and before **`.port:`**). **Sorted unique**, one per line.
On lines containing **`Flags [R]`** (RST packets), print **only** the first whitespace-delimited field (timestamp), **file order**, one per line.
On lines containing **`Flags [S],`**, print the **source endpoint** token after **`IP `** and before **` >`** (e.g. **`192.0.2.10.52414`**). **Sorted unique**, one per line.
questions.solutionMarkdown: SYN-only rows; extract **`IP src > dst`** source token.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Select interface (`-i`), promiscuous vs not, and **permission** model (`sudo`, Linux capabilities `CAP_NET_RAW`).
- Write BPF filters for host/port/protocol; limit size with `-c` / `-w` rotation basics.
- Save pcaps for offline analysis; avoid capturing on untrusted shared Wi‑Fi (privacy note).

## Scope

**In scope:** lab NIC, loopback, or VM tap; BPF expression building blocks; reading **`tcpdump -nn`** one-line summaries (IP, port, TCP flags). **Graded exercises** in this directory parse **saved text** only—no `.pcap` required. **Out of scope:** enterprise SPAN/TAP placement.

## Concept outline

1. **Invocation** — `-n` no DNS in capture path, `-nn` also skip port names, `-v` verbosity levels.
2. **BPF** — `host`, `net`, `port`, `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `vlan`, `and`/`or`, parentheses.
3. **Output** — line vs `-w file.pcap`; `-s 0` snaplen for full payloads; disk fill risk.
4. **Time** — absolute timestamps `-tttt`; high precision where available.
5. **Platform** — `tcpdump` on macOS with `pktap` / `lo0`; Linux `any` pseudo-interface caveats.

## Tooling and alternatives

| Task | Primary | Alternatives |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Capture | `tcpdump` | `dumpcap` (Wireshark CLI, same engine), `tshark -w` (**29**), `ngrep` (regex on payloads), `netsniff-ng` `bpfc`. |
| Live pretty print | `tcpdump -A` | `tshark -V`, `termshark` TUI. |
| USB / Bluetooth | N/A | `usbmon`, `hcidump` — different media. |
| eBPF capture | N/A | `bpftool`, `tcpdump-ebpf` experiments — advanced pointer only. |
